Write your review to `review.md` in this directory using the Write tool. Cite every finding as `head/<path>:<line>` with line numbers taken from the `head/` files. Follow your reviewer skill's output format and end the file with its machine-readable verdict trailer.

<input_guardrails>
<!-- @skill-include: start input_guardrails | hash:d59facd3 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/input_guardrails.md -->
## Pre-Execution Guardrails (mechanized)

Run only if `.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob guardrails.input.enabled false` prints `true`
and env `LOA_GUARDRAILS_ENABLED` is not `false`: write the prompt/args to a temp file (Write tool), then run
`.claude/scripts/guardrails-orchestrator.sh --skill reviewing-code --mode ${LOA_RUN_MODE:-interactive} --file <temp-file>`

| Outcome | Action |
|---------|--------|
| JSON `action: "BLOCK"` | HALT; report the script's `reason` to the user |
| JSON `action: "PROCEED"` or `"WARN"` | Continue (the script logs) |
| Script missing, non-zero exit, or unparseable output | Continue (fail-open) |

Never pass prompt text as a bash argv (quote-blindness FP class) — always via `--file`.
<!-- @skill-include: end input_guardrails -->
</input_guardrails>

# Senior Tech Lead Reviewer

<objective>
Review the sprint implementation for completeness, quality, security and architecture alignment; approve (`All good` + sprint.md checkmarks) or write feedback to `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/engineer-feedback.md`.
</objective>

<permission_grants>
## Permission Grants (MAY — registry-rendered)

Cite the constraint ID when exercising a grant.

<!-- @constraint-generated: start reviewing_code_grants | hash:4e516b2d06e953a5 -->
<!-- DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/constraints.json -->
1. MAY propose alternative approaches that challenge existing architecture during bridge reviews and `/review-sprint`
2. MAY create SPECULATION findings during planning and review skills (`/plan-and-analyze`, `/architect`, `/review-sprint`, bridge reviews) — explicitly excluded from `/implement` and `/audit-sprint`
<!-- @constraint-generated: end reviewing_code_grants -->
</permission_grants>

<adversarial_protocol>
## Adversarial Review Protocol

You are not a rubber stamp; you are a rival.

### Coverage

Report every finding you observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
a separate mechanical step filters, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line` citation of the failing statement — a range
(`file:start-end`) when the defect spans lines — a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. `high` needs a
concrete failing input or exploit path you can name; a check that only *might* misfire is `medium`.

`critical` and `high` findings go under `## Changes Required` and are counted in the
LOA-VERDICT trailer whatever their confidence, except a finding you mark `speculative` with
confidence `low`: it moves to `## Observations` and the trailer records it under `excluded`.
`medium` and `low` findings go under `## Observations` (not blocking, not counted). Never emit a
`## Findings` or `## Issues` heading — `verdict-derive.sh` treats those as blocking on an
approved file. You do not decide the verdict; the counts do.

Entry format (the filter reads the first line of each entry): `- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `path/to/file.py:42` — what fails, and how`; a demoted high reads `- **HIGH** (speculative, confidence: low) …` under `## Observations`.

You MAY approve when every remaining finding sits under `## Observations`, each with a concrete
failure scenario.
</adversarial_protocol>

<zone_constraints>
## Zone Constraints

Zones per the frontmatter `zones:` and CLAUDE.loa.md: the app zone is **Read-only**.
</zone_constraints>

<integrity_precheck>
<!-- @skill-include: start integrity_precheck | hash:47b71a70 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/integrity_precheck.md -->
## Integrity Pre-Check (MANDATORY)

Before ANY operation, verify System Zone integrity:

1. Check config: read `integrity_enforcement` in `.loa.config.yaml`
2. If `strict` and drift detected -> **HALT** and report
3. If `warn` -> Log warning and proceed with caution
<!-- @skill-include: end integrity_precheck -->
</integrity_precheck>

<factual_grounding>
<!-- @skill-include: start factual_grounding | hash:edec7c58 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/factual_grounding.md -->
## Factual Grounding (MANDATORY)

Before ANY synthesis, planning, or recommendation:

1. **Extract quotes**: Pull word-for-word text from source files
2. **Cite explicitly**: `"[exact quote]" (file.md:L45)`
3. **Flag assumptions**: Prefix ungrounded claims with `[ASSUMPTION]`

**Grounded Example:**
```
The SDD specifies "PostgreSQL 15 with pgvector extension" (sdd.md:L123)
```

**Ungrounded Example:**
```
[ASSUMPTION] The database likely needs connection pooling
```
<!-- @skill-include: end factual_grounding -->
</factual_grounding>

<context_discipline>
<!-- @skill-include: start context_discipline | hash:8b81d75a | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/context_discipline.md -->
## Context Discipline

Class: `.run/context-class` (`long` default; `standard` via `LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS=standard` or a
≤200K model). `.claude/protocols/tool-result-clearing.md` — long 20K/50K/30K/150K, standard 2K/5K/3K/15K (single /
accumulated / full file / session) → extract ≤10 files, ≤20 words, file:line to NOTES.md; reason
from it. Big files: `notes-guard.sh read --file F --section <H>` / `--index` first. Start: NOTES.md
"Session Continuity"; end / pre-compaction: update it.
<!-- @skill-include: end context_discipline -->
</context_discipline>

<trajectory_logging>
<!-- @skill-include: start trajectory_logging | hash:e809010f | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/trajectory_logging.md -->
## Trajectory Logging

Log each significant step to `grimoires/loa/a2a/trajectory/{agent}-{date}.jsonl`:

```json
{"timestamp": "...", "agent": "...", "action": "...", "reasoning": "...", "grounding": {...}}
```
<!-- @skill-include: end trajectory_logging -->
</trajectory_logging>

<citation_requirements>
Cite OWASP/CWE for security issues and SDD sections for architecture concerns; quote acceptance criteria and previous feedback when checking them; preserve `integration-context.md` links when present.
</citation_requirements>

<workflow>
## Phase -1: Scope

Parallelise (`parallel_threshold`) when the scope warrants (the lead decides); a sprint with more than 3 tasks splits per task (`<parallel_execution>`).

## Phase 1: Context Gathering

Read, in order:
1. `grimoires/loa/a2a/integration-context.md` if it exists
2. `grimoires/loa/prd.md`, `grimoires/loa/sdd.md`, `grimoires/loa/sprint.md`
3. `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/reviewer.md` — engineer's report
4. `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/engineer-feedback.md` if it exists — your previous feedback (Phase 3)
5. Unless `qmd_context.enabled: false`, run `.claude/scripts/qmd-context-query.sh --query "<changed file paths>" --scope grimoires --budget 1500 --format text` as advisory context; a missing script or no output is a no-op.

## Phase 2: Code Review

Review the code, not the report: read every modified file and its tests (verify the assertions); check the acceptance criteria, readability and conventions, SDD alignment, security (see `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Security) and performance; run the checks below.

**Task kinds**: A `kind: mechanical` task delivered as skill prose or instructions the model re-executes is a MEDIUM (Karpathy ladder); a `kind: operator` task completed unattended without a `decision:unblock` ticket or a DEC row is a MEDIUM.

Tests exist at each declared `### Seams Under Test` seam. For a `/bug` micro-sprint, run `.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh --red <Red commit from reviewer.md> --json -- <test command>`, the command from sprint.md or `red_test.command`, never from reviewer.md, and cite its exit code and verdict for 'Test fails with current code' (see `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Red Test Check).

**Karpathy Principles**: flag violations as `SIMPLICITY:` / `SURGICAL:` / `GOAL-DRIVEN:` feedback; silent assumptions in `reviewer.md` fail Think Before Coding. `SURGICAL:` reads `.run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json` and `.run/karpathy-surgical/<bead>.jsonl` (sprint beads) when present.

**Fast-Gate Parity**: self-checks must match CI's fast gate — verify its formatter check (`prettier --check`, …) and type checker (`tsc --noEmit`, …) ran, per `reviewer.md` or CI. Unrun or failing = `FAST-GATE:` feedback with the weight of a test failure.

## Phase 2.5: Adversarial Cross-Model Review

Runs when `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` write
(`adversarial-review-gate.sh`; override `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes).
Two voices by default (`companion_voice`). One top-level bullet per rejected payload (`rejected_summary`
or `adversarial-rejected-review*.jsonl` rows, whichever is more) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, else
`verdict-derive.sh` fails the trailer. Mechanics: `resources/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md`.
Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never counted.

## Phase 3: Previous Feedback Verification

If `engineer-feedback.md` exists, verify each previous issue in the code (not the report): Resolved, NOT ADDRESSED (blocking) or PARTIALLY ADDRESSED.

## Phase 4: Decision Making

**Approve** when all criteria are met, the work is production-ready and `reviewer.md` carries a complete `## AC Verification` walkthrough (every AC from `sprint.md` verbatim): write `All good` to `engineer-feedback.md` and tick completed tasks in `sprint.md`. **Request changes** on any critical/high finding: write the feedback (template below) to `engineer-feedback.md` and leave `sprint.md` untouched. With zero critical/high, a pile of medium/low is your call (rationale in Overall Assessment).

**Automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED** when
`reviewer.md`'s `## AC Verification` section is missing, shows `✗ Not met` without a
scope-split to a follow-up sprint task, shows `⏸ [ACCEPTED-DEFERRED]` without a matching
Decision Log entry in `grimoires/loa/NOTES.md`, or gives vague evidence for a `Met` claim
instead of `file:line` + a specific symbol.

## Phase 5: Feedback Generation

Use `resources/templates/review-feedback.md`. An approved file reads `All good`, a blank line, then `Sprint {N} has been reviewed and approved. All acceptance criteria met.` — or, with observations, `Observations documented and non-blocking. See Observations below.`

**LOA-VERDICT trailer**: append as the LAST line of `engineer-feedback.md`:
`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved files have
first line exactly `All good` and no `## Changes Required` heading. ONE-WAY rule:
`counts.critical + counts.high > 0` forces `verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does
NOT force APPROVED. `excluded` equals the demoted highs under `## Observations`; a critical
there is a violation.

<adversarial_protocol>
## Adversarial Review Protocol

You are not a rubber stamp; you are a rival.

### Coverage

Report every finding you observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
a separate mechanical step filters, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line` citation of the failing statement — a range
(`file:start-end`) when the defect spans lines — a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. `high` needs a
concrete failing input or exploit path you can name; a check that only *might* misfire is `medium`.

`critical` and `high` findings go under `## Changes Required` and are counted in the
LOA-VERDICT trailer whatever their confidence, except a finding you mark `speculative` with
confidence `low`: it moves to `## Observations` and the trailer records it under `excluded`.
`medium` and `low` findings go under `## Observations` (not blocking, not counted). Never emit a
`## Findings` or `## Issues` heading — `verdict-derive.sh` treats those as blocking on an
approved file. You do not decide the verdict; the counts do.

Entry format (the filter reads the first line of each entry): `- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `path/to/file.py:42` — what fails, and how`; a demoted high reads `- **HIGH** (speculative, confidence: low) …` under `## Observations`.

You MAY approve when every remaining finding sits under `## Observations`, each with a concrete
failure scenario.
</adversarial_protocol>

<workflow>
## Phase -1: Scope

Parallelise (`parallel_threshold`) when the scope warrants (the lead decides); a sprint with more than 3 tasks splits per task (`<parallel_execution>`).

## Phase 1: Context Gathering

Read, in order:
1. `grimoires/loa/a2a/integration-context.md` if it exists
2. `grimoires/loa/prd.md`, `grimoires/loa/sdd.md`, `grimoires/loa/sprint.md`
3. `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/reviewer.md` — engineer's report
4. `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/engineer-feedback.md` if it exists — your previous feedback (Phase 3)
5. Unless `qmd_context.enabled: false`, run `.claude/scripts/qmd-context-query.sh --query "<changed file paths>" --scope grimoires --budget 1500 --format text` as advisory context; a missing script or no output is a no-op.

## Phase 2: Code Review

Review the code, not the report: read every modified file and its tests (verify the assertions); check the acceptance criteria, readability and conventions, SDD alignment, security (see `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Security) and performance; run the checks below.

**Task kinds**: A `kind: mechanical` task delivered as skill prose or instructions the model re-executes is a MEDIUM (Karpathy ladder); a `kind: operator` task completed unattended without a `decision:unblock` ticket or a DEC row is a MEDIUM.

Tests exist at each declared `### Seams Under Test` seam. For a `/bug` micro-sprint, run `.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh --red <Red commit from reviewer.md> --json -- <test command>`, the command from sprint.md or `red_test.command`, never from reviewer.md, and cite its exit code and verdict for 'Test fails with current code' (see `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Red Test Check).

**Karpathy Principles**: flag violations as `SIMPLICITY:` / `SURGICAL:` / `GOAL-DRIVEN:` feedback; silent assumptions in `reviewer.md` fail Think Before Coding. `SURGICAL:` reads `.run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json` and `.run/karpathy-surgical/<bead>.jsonl` (sprint beads) when present.

**Fast-Gate Parity**: self-checks must match CI's fast gate — verify its formatter check (`prettier --check`, …) and type checker (`tsc --noEmit`, …) ran, per `reviewer.md` or CI. Unrun or failing = `FAST-GATE:` feedback with the weight of a test failure.

## Phase 2.5: Adversarial Cross-Model Review

Runs when `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` write
(`adversarial-review-gate.sh`; override `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes).
Two voices by default (`companion_voice`). One top-level bullet per rejected payload (`rejected_summary`
or `adversarial-rejected-review*.jsonl` rows, whichever is more) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, else
`verdict-derive.sh` fails the trailer. Mechanics: `resources/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md`.
Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never counted.

## Phase 3: Previous Feedback Verification

If `engineer-feedback.md` exists, verify each previous issue in the code (not the report): Resolved, NOT ADDRESSED (blocking) or PARTIALLY ADDRESSED.

## Phase 4: Decision Making

**Approve** when all criteria are met, the work is production-ready and `reviewer.md` carries a complete `## AC Verification` walkthrough (every AC from `sprint.md` verbatim): write `All good` to `engineer-feedback.md` and tick completed tasks in `sprint.md`. **Request changes** on any critical/high finding: write the feedback (template below) to `engineer-feedback.md` and leave `sprint.md` untouched. With zero critical/high, a pile of medium/low is your call (rationale in Overall Assessment).

**Automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED** when
`reviewer.md`'s `## AC Verification` section is missing, shows `✗ Not met` without a
scope-split to a follow-up sprint task, shows `⏸ [ACCEPTED-DEFERRED]` without a matching
Decision Log entry in `grimoires/loa/NOTES.md`, or gives vague evidence for a `Met` claim
instead of `file:line` + a specific symbol.

## Phase 5: Feedback Generation

Use `resources/templates/review-feedback.md`. An approved file reads `All good`, a blank line, then `Sprint {N} has been reviewed and approved. All acceptance criteria met.` — or, with observations, `Observations documented and non-blocking. See Observations below.`

**LOA-VERDICT trailer**: append as the LAST line of `engineer-feedback.md`:
`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved files have
first line exactly `All good` and no `## Changes Required` heading. ONE-WAY rule:
`counts.critical + counts.high > 0` forces `verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does
NOT force APPROVED. `excluded` equals the demoted highs under `## Observations`; a critical
there is a violation.

**MUST self-check**: run
`.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh --file grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-{N}/engineer-feedback.md --gate review`
and resolve any inconsistency before finishing.

# Adversarial Cross-Model Review — Phase 2.5 mechanics

Referenced from `reviewing-code/SKILL.md` Phase 2.5. Runs when
`flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true` in `.loa.config.yaml`.

**Objective**: Invoke a cross-model dissenter to catch reviewer blind spots before the final decision.

**Steps**:
1. Invoke adversarial review as the bare call the allowlist grants (`--diff-range`: the script runs the `git diff` itself):
   ```bash
   .claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type review --sprint-id <sprint_id> \
     --diff-range main...HEAD --context-file <concerns file> --json
   ```
2. Read `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-review.json` (Read tool) and parse its findings:
   - If `findings` is empty: continue to Phase 3 — after triaging any rejected payloads (`rejected_summary` or sidecar rows) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, which is mandatory either way
   - If the invocation failed: record it (below) before Phase 3
   - If BLOCKING findings exist: incorporate into Phase 4 decision (forces CHANGES_REQUIRED)
   - If ADVISORY findings only: append as "Cross-Model Observations" section in feedback

**Failure must produce a record.** The `adversarial-review-gate.sh` hook checks this file before any COMPLETED marker is written (when `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled`): it must parse and carry `metadata.type` and `metadata.model` — a `--record-fallback` record names no model, so it never opens the gate: re-run the dissent before the audit completes the sprint (or the operator sets `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes). When `adversarial-review.json` is ABSENT after the script exits — an aborted run leaves none: at start the script moves the previous round's envelope and sidecars aside as `.prev` and never restores them — record the failure with the script itself (a call this skill's allowlist holds; never a hand-written file):

```bash
.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type review --sprint-id <sprint_id> --record-fallback failed --reason "<what happened>"
```

before proceeding. Branch on the `status` line the script prints on stdout, never on exit 2 alone (exit 2 with no status line is a usage error, or a standing envelope that stderr names):

- **An envelope stands after a run that took the run lock** — it is the script's own: triage it; never overwrite it.
- **`failed`** (no envelope: the run aborted) — the call above writes `{"findings": [], "metadata": {"status": "failed", "reason": "<what happened>", "rejected_summary": [], "rejected_sidecars": []}}` under the per-(sprint, gate) run lock. It never writes over an envelope that stands (exit 2), unless the run died before its lock with no status on stdout: what stands is then the previous round's — add `--since <the time on the run's "run started" stderr line>` and an envelope older than that goes aside as `.prev`.
- **`refused_concurrent_run`** (another run — a detached or backgrounded one — holds the run lock; nothing recorded, nothing moved; a `--record-fallback` made meanwhile is refused the same way) — wait until the holding run has exited: an envelope that then stands with a `metadata.timestamp` after your refusal is that run's: triage it as this round's dissent only when its `metadata.scope` is what you asked for (the same `diff_range` and `diff_oids` as your refusal's own `metadata.scope` — the commits, not just the ref names — and `run_tag` null: a chunk driver's tagged run reviewed one chunk); otherwise, or when none stands, run again.
- **`workdir_unavailable`, `nothing_to_review`, `budget_exceeded`, `diff_range_failed`** (the range's `git diff` failed — e.g. a base ref a shallow clone lacks; `workdir_unavailable` with `metadata.path` is a previous round's file that could not be moved aside — make the a2a directory writable; written BEFORE the run lock, or with it released; non-zero exit, stdout only; nothing moved aside, so any envelope at the path is the PREVIOUS run's and never this round's evidence) — record it: `--record-fallback <the status> --reason "<its stdout line>" --since <the run started time>` (it never displaces an envelope written after that) moves that envelope and its `adversarial-rejected-review*.jsonl` sidecars aside as `<name>.prev` (as a run does at start) before it writes, so `verdict-derive.sh` judges this round's record, not the last round's.

A record names what it moved aside (`metadata.displaced`: status, timestamp, findings, rejected); `verdict-derive.sh` warns when that held findings. `verdict-derive.sh` never scans `.prev` files (they are the previous round's evidence, already triaged in that round's feedback) and reports `.prev` files with NO envelope as a `dissent_aborted` violation, which a fallback record clears; `rejected_sidecars: []` does not silence a canonical `adversarial-rejected-review*.jsonl` beside it — that is this run's own partial work, counted whether listed or not: triage its rows under `## Rejected dissent payloads`.

Do NOT silently skip — the gate hook has no way to distinguish "not attempted" from "attempted and failed", and the distinction matters for audit trail.

**Parameter Derivation**:

|-----------------|-----------------|
| `--sprint-id` | From SKILL invocation args, resolved via ledger |
| `--diff-range` | `main...HEAD` (the script runs `git diff`) |
| `--context-file` | Reviewer's Phase 2 concern notes, written (Write tool) to `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/reviewer-concerns.md` |
| `--model` | From `flatline_protocol.code_review.model` config |
| `--budget` | From `flatline_protocol.code_review.budget_cents` config |
| `--timeout` | From `flatline_protocol.code_review.timeout_seconds` config |

**Output**: Findings written to `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-review.json`

**Failure mode**: If adversarial review is unavailable (timeout, API error, budget exceeded), record it as above, then proceed with single-model assessment and log warning. No DEGRADED marker for review (only audit).

## Two voices and the rejected-payload contract (cycle-126 FR-2)

**Companion voice (D-2.1).** Every dissent plans a second chain from the *other* provider
family — the primary configured on the block decides: any primary outside the Anthropic family (OpenAI,
Google, xAI, unknown) gets the Anthropic chain (`opus` → `claude-headless`), an Anthropic-family primary gets the OpenAI chain
(`gpt-5.5` → `codex-headless`; KF-002 keeps `gpt-5.5-pro` out of the default). Credential *presence* (env → `.env.local` →
`.env`; the value is never read) decides only where the companion chain starts — with no key it
starts at the CLI hop. Both chains walk in parallel; the two completed envelopes are aggregated
(`verdict_quality.voices_succeeded_ids` lists only completed voices). `companion_voice.status` is `succeeded`,
`failed` or `fold_failed`; `verdict_quality.voices_planned` counts the aggregated envelopes — 2 whenever the companion ran,
completed or not (a failed one is listed in `voices_dropped`) — except a failed companion whose id is one of the primary's
succeeded voices: INV-5 lets it feed no envelope, so `voices_planned` stays 1 and `companion_voice` is its only record; a `duplicate_voice` companion contributes none, and a
dropped entry naming the model the companion answered with is removed (INV-5). `companion_voice.counted_as`
(`independent_voice`, `duplicate_voice`, `sole_voice` — the primary never answered) names the outcome, and `planned: false` with a `reason` (`no_workdir`, `no_route`,
`prompt_copy_failed`) is a companion that never started; a bare `planned: false` is the opt-out. The
companion's findings arrive re-numbered `DISS-C-NNN` with a `voice` field; the primary's carry
`voice` too. `metadata.companion_voice` records `{planned, family, family_basis, chain, model,
status: succeeded|failed|fold_failed, failure_class: auth|model_unavailable|quota|timeout|lock_wait|malformed|null,
cost_cents, attempts}`; a companion whose chain fails is a dropped voice (degraded for an audit,
never blocking a review). Opt-out per block: `flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice: false`
(the YAML boolean spellings in any case; a value that is none of them is reported and the voice stays on).

**Tolerant schema (D-2.2).** A finding missing only `failure_mode` is no longer dropped: the
first sentence of its `description` (≤ 200 chars) becomes `failure_mode` and the finding is
marked `failure_mode_derived: true` (a missing `id` is filled positionally, `id_derived: true`).
Severity, category and description are never touched. Payloads that still fail go to the
sidecar (`adversarial-rejected-<type>.jsonl`, `-companion` suffix for the second voice) **and**
to `metadata.rejected_summary[]` as `{index, severity, title, title_derived, anchor, reason, description_head}`.

| `--sprint-id` | From SKILL invocation args, resolved via ledger |
| `--diff-range` | `main...HEAD` (the script runs `git diff`) |
| `--context-file` | Reviewer's Phase 2 concern notes, written (Write tool) to `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/reviewer-concerns.md` |
| `--model` | From `flatline_protocol.code_review.model` config |
| `--budget` | From `flatline_protocol.code_review.budget_cents` config |
| `--timeout` | From `flatline_protocol.code_review.timeout_seconds` config |

**Output**: Findings written to `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-review.json`

**Failure mode**: If adversarial review is unavailable (timeout, API error, budget exceeded), record it as above, then proceed with single-model assessment and log warning. No DEGRADED marker for review (only audit).

## Two voices and the rejected-payload contract (cycle-126 FR-2)

**Companion voice (D-2.1).** Every dissent plans a second chain from the *other* provider
family — the primary configured on the block decides: any primary outside the Anthropic family (OpenAI,
Google, xAI, unknown) gets the Anthropic chain (`opus` → `claude-headless`), an Anthropic-family primary gets the OpenAI chain
(`gpt-5.5` → `codex-headless`; KF-002 keeps `gpt-5.5-pro` out of the default). Credential *presence* (env → `.env.local` →
`.env`; the value is never read) decides only where the companion chain starts — with no key it
starts at the CLI hop. Both chains walk in parallel; the two completed envelopes are aggregated
(`verdict_quality.voices_succeeded_ids` lists only completed voices). `companion_voice.status` is `succeeded`,
`failed` or `fold_failed`; `verdict_quality.voices_planned` counts the aggregated envelopes — 2 whenever the companion ran,
completed or not (a failed one is listed in `voices_dropped`) — except a failed companion whose id is one of the primary's
succeeded voices: INV-5 lets it feed no envelope, so `voices_planned` stays 1 and `companion_voice` is its only record; a `duplicate_voice` companion contributes none, and a
dropped entry naming the model the companion answered with is removed (INV-5). `companion_voice.counted_as`
(`independent_voice`, `duplicate_voice`, `sole_voice` — the primary never answered) names the outcome, and `planned: false` with a `reason` (`no_workdir`, `no_route`,
`prompt_copy_failed`) is a companion that never started; a bare `planned: false` is the opt-out. The
companion's findings arrive re-numbered `DISS-C-NNN` with a `voice` field; the primary's carry
`voice` too. `metadata.companion_voice` records `{planned, family, family_basis, chain, model,
status: succeeded|failed|fold_failed, failure_class: auth|model_unavailable|quota|timeout|lock_wait|malformed|null,
cost_cents, attempts}`; a companion whose chain fails is a dropped voice (degraded for an audit,
never blocking a review). Opt-out per block: `flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice: false`
(the YAML boolean spellings in any case; a value that is none of them is reported and the voice stays on).

**Tolerant schema (D-2.2).** A finding missing only `failure_mode` is no longer dropped: the
first sentence of its `description` (≤ 200 chars) becomes `failure_mode` and the finding is
marked `failure_mode_derived: true` (a missing `id` is filled positionally, `id_derived: true`).
Severity, category and description are never touched. Payloads that still fail go to the
sidecar (`adversarial-rejected-<type>.jsonl`, `-companion` suffix for the second voice) **and**
to `metadata.rejected_summary[]` as `{index, severity, title, title_derived, anchor, reason, description_head}`.

    42	#                                 LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false exported in the CALLING shell
    43	#                                 and written to $ARM_ENV_FILE (KEY=VALUE lines) when that is set
    44	#         flatline: false         flatline_protocol.enabled=false
    45	#         sprint_plan: false, context_resets: false
    46	#                                 phase-set edits owned by the pipeline executor; recorded as
    47	#                                 evidence here (the single-skill executor refuses them itself)
    48	#   regen_sandbox_manifest <ws>
    49	#       writes <ws>/.claude/checksums.json {generated, algorithm: sha256, files} over
    50	#       every regular file under <ws>/.claude except overrides/ and the manifest
    51	#       itself (LC_ALL=C order, sha256). tools/gen-checksums.sh (in the
    52	#       prompt tree, $EVAL_PROMPT_TREE) is used instead when it exists AND <ws> is a
    53	#       git repository tracking .claude files (it lists `git ls-files`). No .claude/
    54	#       (loa_mount: false) → manifest_sha256=none, exit 0. Prints manifest_sha256=<hex>.
    55	#   check_fixture_path_rule <fixture_dir>
    56	#       exit 2 (offending paths on stderr) when the fixture's top level holds
    57	#       .claude, CLAUDE.md, .loa.config.yaml, grimoires or .run — the mount owns
    58	#       those paths (DEC-0396); exit 0 otherwise.
    59	#   write_sandbox_grimoire <ws> <task_yaml> <arm> <sprint_label>
    60	#       grimoires/loa/ledger.json (one active cycle, <sprint_label> planned, global 1;
    61	#       the ledger-lib.sh schema), NOTES.md (header only), context/task-brief.md (the
    62	#       task's agent-facing `criterion` + the TASK.md next to task.yaml),
    63	#       a2a/<sprint_label>/ (empty); review-catch tasks also get a one-sprint
    64	#       grimoires/loa/sprint.md naming pr/head.diff and a2a/<sprint_label>/reviewer.md
    65	#       carrying pr/PR.md (sandbox copy, else the corpus fixture's). An arm whose
    66	#       toggles carry sprint_plan: false (resolved from $LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE, default
    67	#       evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml) gets NO sprint.md. Build tasks leave sprint.md
    68	#       to the PLAN phase. Nothing written names the arm.
    69	#   init_sandbox_beads <ws> <task_title>

    75	# Hashing is Python hashlib (_sm_sha256), never .claude/ code: see _sm_sha256.
    76	# Callers source this file by a literal relative path (no variable expansion

    81	# else they go to the descriptor in SANDBOX_MOUNT_EVIDENCE_FD (default 1).
    82	# resolve_arm_toggles prints JSON on stdout and no evidence.
    83	#

    94	_sm_err() { echo "ERROR: $*" >&2; }
    95	
    96	# _sm_sha256 <file>... prints "<hex>  <file>" lines, the sha256sum output shape.
    97	# Python hashlib, not compat-lib's sha256_portable: the eval workflow runs the
    98	# harness as the trusted copy against a PR's .claude/, so no harness script
    99	# sources .claude/ code (eval.yml "Validate grader trust boundary"); run-arms.sh
   100	# hashes the corpus the same way.
   101	_sm_sha256() {
   102	  python3 -I -c '
   103	import hashlib, sys
   104	for p in sys.argv[1:]:
   105	    h = hashlib.sha256()
   106	    with open(p, "rb") as f:
   107	        for b in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
   108	            h.update(b)
   109	    print(h.hexdigest() + "  " + p)' "$@"
   110	}

   112	# _sm_evidence <key> <value> — one key=value line to the evidence sink.
   113	_sm_evidence() {
   114	  local line="$1=${2//$'\n'/ }"
   115	  if [[ -n "${ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE:-}" ]]; then
   116	    printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE"
   117	  else
   118	    local fd="${SANDBOX_MOUNT_EVIDENCE_FD:-1}"
   119	    [[ "$fd" =~ ^[0-9]$ ]] || fd=1
   120	    printf '%s\n' "$line" >&"$fd"
   121	  fi
   122	}

   163	  [[ "$arm" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$ ]] || { _sm_err "invalid arm id '$arm'"; return 2; }
   164	  local found=0 entry=""
   165	  if [[ -n "$suite_file" && -f "$suite_file" ]]; then
   166	    # an unreadable suite file reads as "not declared" (cycle-129 behaviour: baseline still resolves to {})
   167	    entry="$(ARM="$arm" yq -o=json -I=0 '[((.arms // [])[]), ((.ab.arms // [])[])] | map(select(.id == strenv(ARM))) | .[0] // null' "$suite_file" 2>/dev/null)" \
   168	      || entry=""
   169	    [[ -n "$entry" && "$entry" != "null" ]] && found=1

   187	# Remove the markdown section that starts at the exact heading line $2 (up to
   188	# the next level-2 heading) from file $1. Prints the number of lines removed.
   189	_sm_drop_md_section() {
   190	  local f="$1" heading="$2" tmpdir="$3" tmp
   191	  tmp="$(mktemp "$tmpdir/.arm.XXXXXX")"
   192	  awk -v h="$heading" '
   193	    $0 == h { skip = 1; n++; next }
   194	    skip && /^## / { skip = 0 }
   195	    skip { n++; next }
   196	    { print }
   197	    END { print n + 0 > "/dev/stderr" }' "$f" > "$tmp" 2> "$tmp.n"
   198	  mv "$tmp" "$f"
   199	  cat "$tmp.n"; rm -f "$tmp.n"
   200	}
   201	
   202	# Remove the first blank-line-delimited paragraph of $1 that contains one of
   203	# the needles (tried in order, case-insensitive). Writes the removed text to
   204	# $2; exit 1 when no needle matches.
   205	_sm_drop_paragraph() {
   206	  python3 -I - "$1" "$2" "look for what the review did not" "Confirm the review's demotions independently" <<'PY'
   207	import re, sys
   208	path, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   209	text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
   210	paras = re.split(r"(\n[ \t]*\n)", text)
   211	for needle in sys.argv[3:]:
   212	    for i in range(0, len(paras), 2):
   213	        if needle.lower() in paras[i].lower():
   214	            removed = paras[i]
   215	            # drop the paragraph and the separator that follows it
   216	            del paras[i:i + 2]
   217	            open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("".join(paras))
   218	            open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(removed + "\n")
   219	            sys.exit(0)
   220	sys.exit(1)
   221	PY
   222	}

   224	# Strip every `effort:` line from the YAML frontmatter of file $1 (frontmatter
   225	# = line 1 `---` up to the next `---`). Prints 1 when a line was removed, else 0.
   226	_sm_strip_frontmatter_effort() {
   227	  local f="$1" tmp
   228	  tmp="$(mktemp "$f.XXXXXX")"
   229	  awk '
   230	    NR == 1 && $0 == "---" { fm = 1; print; next }
   231	    fm == 1 && $0 == "---" { fm = 2; print; next }
   232	    fm == 1 && /^effort:/ { n++; next }
   233	    { print }
   234	    END { print (n > 0 ? 1 : 0) > "/dev/stderr" }' "$f" > "$tmp" 2> "$tmp.n"
   235	  cat "$tmp" > "$f"; rm -f "$tmp"
   236	  cat "$tmp.n"; rm -f "$tmp.n"
   237	}
   238	
   239	# 0 when file $1's frontmatter still carries an `effort:` line.
   240	_sm_frontmatter_has_effort() {
   241	  awk 'NR == 1 && $0 != "---" { exit 1 } NR > 1 && $0 == "---" { exit 1 } NR > 1 && /^effort:/ { found = 1; exit 0 } END { exit (found ? 0 : 1) }' "$1"
   242	}

   244	_sm_cfg_set_false() {  # _sm_cfg_set_false <cfg> <yq-path>... ; verifies each
   245	  local cfg="$1"; shift
   246	  [[ -f "$cfg" ]] || : > "$cfg"
   247	  local p
   248	  for p in "$@"; do
   249	    P="$p" yq -i 'eval(strenv(P)) = false' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null || return 1
   250	    [[ "$(P="$p" yq -r 'eval(strenv(P))' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null)" == "false" ]] || return 1
   251	  done
   252	  return 0
   253	}

   376	regen_sandbox_manifest() {
   377	  local ws="$1"
   378	  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
   379	  if [[ ! -d "$ws/.claude" ]]; then
   380	    _sm_evidence manifest_sha256 "none"
   381	    return 0
   382	  fi
   383	  local out="$ws/.claude/checksums.json" tool="${EVAL_PROMPT_TREE:-$_SM_REPO_ROOT}/tools/gen-checksums.sh" how="inline"
   384	  if [[ -x "$tool" ]] && git -C "$ws" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1 \
   385	     && [[ -n "$(git -C "$ws" ls-files .claude 2>/dev/null | head -1)" ]]; then
   386	    "$tool" --root "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: $tool --root $ws failed"; return 2; }
   387	    how="gen-checksums.sh"
   388	  else
   389	    local list="$ws/.eval/.manifest-files" sums="$ws/.eval/.manifest-sums"
   390	    mkdir -p "$ws/.eval"
   391	    ( cd "$ws" && find .claude -type f ! -path '.claude/overrides/*' ! -path '.claude/checksums.json' -print ) \
   392	      | LC_ALL=C sort > "$list"
   393	    if grep -q '\\' "$list"; then _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: a path under .claude/ holds a backslash"; rm -f "$list"; return 2; fi
   394	    : > "$sums"
   395	    local -a batch=()
   396	    local f
   397	    while IFS= read -r f; do
   398	      batch+=("$f")
   399	      if [[ ${#batch[@]} -ge 200 ]]; then
   400	        ( cd "$ws" && _sm_sha256 "${batch[@]}" ) >> "$sums" || { _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: hashing failed"; return 2; }
   401	        batch=()
   402	      fi
   403	    done < "$list"
   404	    if [[ ${#batch[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
   405	      ( cd "$ws" && _sm_sha256 "${batch[@]}" ) >> "$sums" || { _sm_err "regen_sandbox_manifest: hashing failed"; return 2; }
   406	    fi

     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# pipeline-run.sh — the cycle-130 ablation pipeline executor (SDD §1.4 D-4.1 … D-4.10, §5.6)
     4	#
     5	# Runs ONE task under ONE arm: materialises a sandbox repository (the task's
     6	# fixture tree, or the review-catch PR under pr/, plus the Loa mount from the
     7	# pinned --source-tree), then drives Loa's phases as separate `claude -p`
     8	# sessions inside it, records every phase, enforces the per-run cap and writes
     9	# meta/pipeline.json. One executor serves every task type (D-4.1):
    10	#   review-catch                      REVIEW → AUDIT
    11	#   bug-fix | refactor | feature-build PLAN → IMPLEMENT → REVIEW → FIX? → AUDIT → FIX?
    12	# A FIX runs only when the gate before it wrote a CHANGES_REQUIRED LOA-VERDICT
    13	# trailer (the last `<!-- LOA-VERDICT {…} -->` line of
    14	# grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/engineer-feedback.md resp. auditor-sprint-feedback.md);
    15	# a FIX that does not run is recorded `skipped: true`.
    16	# Arms edit the phase set (D-4.2): `sprint_plan: false` drops PLAN; `gates: false`
    17	# ends after IMPLEMENT; `loa_mount: false` runs one BARE session (no mount);
    18	# `flatline: false` keeps PLAN with the Flatline step off; `context_resets: false`
    19	# runs PLAN, IMPLEMENT and FIX as ONE implementer session (`--resume <session_id>`
    20	# from the first session's system/init event) while REVIEW and AUDIT stay separate.
    21	# The suite's `phase_sets[<review-catch|build>]` and an arm's `phases` override the
    22	# default phase list; the toggle edits above apply on top.
    23	#
    24	# Usage:
    25	#   pipeline-run.sh --task-yaml F --arm ID --run-dir D --run-id R --trial N \
    26	#                   --source-tree DIR --suite-file F [--max-run-usd 12] \
    27	#                   [--executor container|host] [--image IMG] [--claude-bin B] \
    28	#                   [--docker-bin D] [--phase-models JSON] [--phase-timeouts JSON] [--dry-run]
    29	#
    30	# Options:
    31	#   --task-yaml F       task.yaml (SDD §3.2); its directory holds TASK.md
    32	#   --arm ID            arm id declared in the suite file (`arms[].id`)
    33	#   --run-dir D         run directory to create (must not exist or be empty);
    34	#                       alias --workspace
    35	#   --run-id R          run id recorded in pipeline.json
    36	#   --trial N           trial number
    37	#   --source-tree DIR   the pinned Loa tree the mount is copied from
    38	#   --suite-file F      evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml (read with yq -o=json)
    39	#   --max-run-usd USD   per-run cap (default 12; config evals.ablation.run_cap_usd)

    48	# Run directory layout (DEC-0413 — the grader never reads meta/):
    49	#   sandbox/     the agent's tree (its own .git initialised at `base`)
    50	#   snapshots/   <label>.bundle + index.json ({IMPLEMENT|FIX1|FIX2: commit}) after
    51	#                IMPLEMENT and each FIX
    52	#   transcripts/ events-<label>.jsonl (stream-json), stderr-<label>.log
    53	#   eval/        model-invoke.jsonl, cost-ledger.jsonl (copied out of
    54	#                sandbox/.eval/ after every phase), adversarial-*.json
    55	#   meta/        pipeline.json, phase-<label>.argv.json (argv + captured env),
    56	#                prompt-<label>.md, arm, arm-evidence.txt, arm-env, refused.json,
    57	#                home/ (container mode: the per-run HOME; deleted at exit)
    58	#
    59	# Session (D-4.3, DEC-0394 as amended, DEC-0412): `claude -p <prompt> --output-format
    60	# stream-json --verbose --model <id> --permission-mode bypassPermissions
    61	# --dangerously-skip-permissions --setting-sources project --tools <list>
    62	# --max-turns <cap> [--effort <v>] [--resume <id>]`, cwd sandbox/, with exactly this
    63	# environment: PATH HOME LANG LC_ALL TERM TMPDIR CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK
    64	# CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL LOA_MODELINV_LOG_PATH LOA_COST_LEDGER_PATH
    65	# GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GH_CONFIG_DIR=<sandbox/.eval/gh-empty>,
    66	# the Bedrock route's pass-through keys when set in the driver's environment
    67	# (AWS_REGION AWS_DEFAULT_REGION AWS_PROFILE AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK
    68	# ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_REGION_PREFIX ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_{OPUS,SONNET,HAIKU}_MODEL), and the
    69	# arm's LOA_* variables (LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false for gates: false).
    70	# A python3 -I exec shim closes every descriptor above 2 and keeps exactly those keys;
    71	# values reach it through the environment, never argv, so AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK
    72	# appears in no argv, capture or log (phase-<label>.argv.json records it as "<set>").
    73	# `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=15` bounds the CLI.
    74	# Container mode (D-4.9, DEC-0411 as amended) runs the same command inside
    75	#   docker run --rm --name <n> --user <uid>:<gid> --network bridge --read-only
    76	#     --tmpfs /tmp:rw,size=1g --pids-limit 512 --memory 4g --cpus 2
    77	#     -v <run>/sandbox:/workspace:rw -v <run>/meta/home:/home/evaluser:rw
    78	#     -w /workspace -e <KEY=value…> -e AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK <image> python3 -I -c <shim> … claude …
    79	# Exactly two mounts. meta/home/ (mode 0700) holds copies of $HOME/.codex/{auth.json,
    80	# config.toml} when present and empty .claude/ and .aws/; the CLI's session store
    81	# lives there for the whole run, so A6's --resume works across phases. No ~/.claude
    82	# file is ever copied. The directory is deleted at exit and on interrupt.
    83	# image_digest = the image's RepoDigest or id (container), else the fingerprint (host).
    84	# Versions: `fingerprint` is computed from the HOST toolchain; in container mode the
    85	# toolchain that runs the phases is the image's (Claude Code 2.1.299, codex 0.137.0 by
    86	# Dockerfile.ablation), so image_digest identifies the batch's versions. On 2026-10-15
    87	# the host CLI was 2.1.300 while the image pins 2.1.299; every arm runs in the container.
    88	#
    89	# Cap and watchdog (D-4.6, D-4.10): while a phase runs the driver re-prices the
    90	# stream's assistant-turn usage every $LOA_EVAL_WATCHDOG_POLL_S seconds (default 1)
    91	# from per-token prices fetched once per model (pricing.py; $LOA_EVAL_PRICING_JSON
    92	# overrides) and SIGTERMs the phase when spent + estimate ≥ the cap (cap_turn
    93	# recorded). After each phase the result's total_cost_usd (authoritative) plus the
    94	# sandbox cost-ledger rows written during the phase are added; ≥ cap → cap_failure.
    95	#
    96	# Exit codes:
    97	#   0  finished (any verdict)                                   status completed
    98	#   1  agent error: a phase exited non-zero or timed out        status agent_error
    99	#   2  infrastructure: usage, refused arm/type, mount/toggle failure, CLI/docker
   100	#      or image missing, fixture path rule, leak guard          status infrastructure_error

   102	#   4  interrupted (SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP to the driver, or a phase killed from

   104	# pipeline.json is written for every exit except usage errors and --dry-run; it is

   107	#
   108	# Env: EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN, EVAL_DOCKER_BIN, LOA_EVAL_PHASE_MODELS, LOA_EVAL_PRICING_JSON,

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# pipeline-run.sh — the cycle-130 ablation pipeline executor (SDD §1.4 D-4.1 … D-4.10, §5.6)
     4	#
     5	# Runs ONE task under ONE arm: materialises a sandbox repository (the task's
     6	# fixture tree, or the review-catch PR under pr/, plus the Loa mount from the
     7	# pinned --source-tree), then drives Loa's phases as separate `claude -p`
     8	# sessions inside it, records every phase, enforces the per-run cap and writes
     9	# meta/pipeline.json. One executor serves every task type (D-4.1):
    10	#   review-catch                      REVIEW → AUDIT
    11	#   bug-fix | refactor | feature-build PLAN → IMPLEMENT → REVIEW → FIX? → AUDIT → FIX?
    12	# A FIX runs only when the gate before it wrote a CHANGES_REQUIRED LOA-VERDICT
    13	# trailer (the last `<!-- LOA-VERDICT {…} -->` line of
    14	# grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/engineer-feedback.md resp. auditor-sprint-feedback.md);
    15	# a FIX that does not run is recorded `skipped: true`.
    16	# Arms edit the phase set (D-4.2): `sprint_plan: false` drops PLAN; `gates: false`
    17	# ends after IMPLEMENT; `loa_mount: false` runs one BARE session (no mount);
    18	# `flatline: false` keeps PLAN with the Flatline step off; `context_resets: false`
    19	# runs PLAN, IMPLEMENT and FIX as ONE implementer session (`--resume <session_id>`
    20	# from the first session's system/init event) while REVIEW and AUDIT stay separate.
    21	# The suite's `phase_sets[<review-catch|build>]` and an arm's `phases` override the
    22	# default phase list; the toggle edits above apply on top.
    23	#
    24	# Usage:
    25	#   pipeline-run.sh --task-yaml F --arm ID --run-dir D --run-id R --trial N \
    26	#                   --source-tree DIR --suite-file F [--max-run-usd 12] \
    27	#                   [--executor container|host] [--image IMG] [--claude-bin B] \
    28	#                   [--docker-bin D] [--phase-models JSON] [--phase-timeouts JSON] [--dry-run]
    29	#
    30	# Options:
    31	#   --task-yaml F       task.yaml (SDD §3.2); its directory holds TASK.md
    32	#   --arm ID            arm id declared in the suite file (`arms[].id`)
    33	#   --run-dir D         run directory to create (must not exist or be empty);
    34	#                       alias --workspace
    35	#   --run-id R          run id recorded in pipeline.json
    36	#   --trial N           trial number
    37	#   --source-tree DIR   the pinned Loa tree the mount is copied from
    38	#   --suite-file F      evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml (read with yq -o=json)
    39	#   --max-run-usd USD   per-run cap (default 12; config evals.ablation.run_cap_usd)
    40	#   --executor MODE     container (default; DEC-0411) or host

    17	#   --allow-partial   passed to validate-suite.sh (fewer than four tasks per type)
    18	#   --suite-file F    passed to validate-suite.sh

    21	# or `freeze: OK — N files match MANIFEST.sha256 (sha256 …)`; on drift every
    22	# changed / added / removed path on its own line.

     3	# fingerprint.sh — toolchain fingerprint for ablation runs (cycle-130 FR-4, SDD A11 / DEC-0389)
     4	#
     5	# Prints `fp:<sha256>` over the LC_ALL=C-sorted `tool=version` lines of the
     6	# toolchain an ablation run depends on (claude, codex, python3, node, yq, jq,
     7	# bats, git, docker) plus `source_tree=<HEAD of --source-tree>`. A tool that is
     8	# not installed reads `tool=absent`, so a missing tool changes the fingerprint
     9	# instead of failing the run. The value fills `image_digest` in host mode and
    10	# `fingerprint` in every mode (MANIFEST.json, pipeline.json, runs.jsonl). It reads the
    11	# HOST toolchain: in container mode the phases run on the image's toolchain, and the
    12	# image digest (not this value) identifies the batch's versions (on 2026-10-15 the host
    13	# CLI was 2.1.300 while Dockerfile.ablation pins 2.1.299).
    14	#
    15	# Usage:
    16	#   fingerprint.sh [--source-tree DIR] [--claude-bin B] [--bats-bin B] [--json]
    17	#
    18	# Options:
    19	#   --source-tree DIR  the pinned Loa tree; its `git rev-parse HEAD` is folded in
    20	#                      (`none` when absent or not a git tree)
    21	#   --claude-bin B     the CLI executable (default: $EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN, else claude)
    22	#   --bats-bin B       bats executable (default: bats on PATH, else the operator's
    23	#                      ~/.local/dotfiles/tools/diff-so-fancy/test/bats/bin/bats)
    24	#   --json             print {fingerprint, tools{}, source_tree, lines[]} instead
    25	#

    27	#   0  printed
    28	#   2  usage error

    31	# =============================================================================
    32	set -euo pipefail
    33	export LC_ALL=C
    34	
    35	# Hashing is Python hashlib: no harness script sources .claude/ code (eval.yml
    36	# "Validate grader trust boundary").

    39	CLAUDE_BIN="${EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN:-claude}"
    40	BATS_BIN="${LOA_EVAL_BATS_BIN:-}"

    42	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    43	  case "$1" in
    44	    --source-tree) SOURCE_TREE="${2:?--source-tree needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
    45	    --claude-bin)  CLAUDE_BIN="${2:?--claude-bin needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
    46	    --bats-bin)    BATS_BIN="${2:?--bats-bin needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
    47	    --json)        JSON=true; shift ;;
    48	    -h|--help)     sed -n '2,28p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;

    50	  esac
    51	done

    53	  if command -v bats >/dev/null 2>&1; then BATS_BIN=bats
    54	  else BATS_BIN="$HOME/.local/dotfiles/tools/diff-so-fancy/test/bats/bin/bats"; fi
    55	fi

    57	# first line of `<bin> <args>`, whitespace collapsed; `absent` when not runnable

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# freeze.sh — cycle-130 ablation suite freeze (SDD §5.13, DEC-0404, DEC-0414)
     4	#
     5	# Writes or verifies <root>/MANIFEST.sha256, the suite's frozen identity: one
     6	# "<sha256>  <relpath>" line per file under <root>/tasks/ (and <root>/smoke/
     7	# with --smoke), relpath relative to the root, LC_ALL=C sorted, sha256 (Python
     8	# hashlib: no harness script sources .claude/ code, eval.yml trust boundary).
     9	# validate-suite.sh runs first; an invalid suite is never frozen or accepted.
    10	#
    11	# Usage:
    12	#   freeze.sh [--root DIR] [--smoke] [--check] [--allow-partial] [--suite-file F]
    13	#
    14	#   --root DIR        suite root (default grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0)
    15	#   --smoke           cover smoke/ too (passed to the validator as well)
    16	#   --check           recompute and compare with MANIFEST.sha256; write nothing
    17	#   --allow-partial   passed to validate-suite.sh (fewer than four tasks per type)
    18	#   --suite-file F    passed to validate-suite.sh
    19	#
    20	# Output: `freeze: wrote MANIFEST.sha256 (N files, sha256 <digest of the manifest>)`
    21	# or `freeze: OK — N files match MANIFEST.sha256 (sha256 …)`; on drift every
    22	# changed / added / removed path on its own line.
    23	#
    24	# Exit: 0 written / matches; 1 drift, missing manifest under --check, or the
    25	#       validator found violations; 2 usage.
    26	# Tested by evals/tests/freeze.bats.
    27	# =============================================================================
    28	set -euo pipefail
    29	export LC_ALL=C
    30	
    31	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    32	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    33	
    34	ROOT="$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0"
    35	CHECK=false SMOKE=false
    36	VARGS=()
    37	
    38	usage() { sed -n '2,/^# =====.*$/p' "$0" | sed -n '2,26p' | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2; }
    39	die() { echo "freeze: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    40	
    41	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    42	  case "$1" in
    43	    --root) ROOT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    44	    --smoke) SMOKE=true; VARGS+=(--smoke); shift ;;
    45	    --check) CHECK=true; shift ;;
    46	    --allow-partial) VARGS+=(--allow-partial); shift ;;
    47	    --suite-file) [[ -n "${2:-}" ]] || die "--suite-file needs a path"; VARGS+=(--suite-file "$2"); shift 2 ;;
    48	    --help|-h) usage ;;
    49	    *) die "unknown option: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    50	  esac
    51	done
    52	[[ -n "$ROOT" && -d "$ROOT" ]] || die "suite root not found: ${ROOT:-<empty>}"
    53	ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd)"
    54	MANIFEST="$ROOT/MANIFEST.sha256"
    55	
    56	vrc=0
    57	"$SCRIPT_DIR/validate-suite.sh" --root "$ROOT" ${VARGS[@]+"${VARGS[@]}"} || vrc=$?
    58	if [[ $vrc -eq 1 ]]; then echo "freeze: refused — the suite does not validate" >&2; exit 1; fi
    59	[[ $vrc -eq 0 ]] || die "validate-suite.sh failed (exit $vrc)"
    60	
    61	# compute_manifest <out> — the manifest body for the current tree.
    62	compute_manifest() {
    63	  local out="$1" list dirs=(tasks)
    64	  [[ "$SMOKE" == "true" ]] && dirs+=(smoke)
    65	  list="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/freeze-list.XXXXXX")"
    66	  local d
    67	  for d in "${dirs[@]}"; do
    68	    [[ -d "$ROOT/$d" ]] || continue
    69	    ( cd "$ROOT" && find "$d" -type f -print )
    70	  done | LC_ALL=C sort > "$list"
    71	  if grep -q '\\' "$list"; then rm -f "$list"; die "a path under the suite holds a backslash"; fi
    72	  python3 -I - "$ROOT" "$list" > "$out" <<'PY' || { rm -f "$list"; die "hashing failed"; }
    73	import hashlib, os, sys
    74	root, listing = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    75	for rel in open(listing, encoding="utf-8").read().splitlines():
    76	    if not rel:
    77	        continue
    78	    h = hashlib.sha256()
    79	    with open(os.path.join(root, rel), "rb") as f:
    80	        for b in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
    81	            h.update(b)
    82	    print(h.hexdigest() + "  " + rel)
    83	PY
    84	  rm -f "$list"
    85	}
    86	digest_of() { python3 -I -c 'import hashlib, sys; print(hashlib.sha256(open(sys.argv[1], "rb").read()).hexdigest())' "$1"; }
    87	
    88	TMP="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/freeze.XXXXXX")"
    89	trap 'rm -f "$TMP"' EXIT
    90	compute_manifest "$TMP"
    91	n="$(grep -c . "$TMP" || true)"
    92	
    93	if [[ "$CHECK" == "true" ]]; then
    94	  [[ -f "$MANIFEST" ]] || { echo "freeze: no MANIFEST.sha256 in $ROOT (run freeze.sh first)" >&2; exit 1; }
    95	  if cmp -s "$TMP" "$MANIFEST"; then
    96	    echo "freeze: OK — $n files match MANIFEST.sha256 (sha256 $(digest_of "$MANIFEST"))"
    97	    exit 0
    98	  fi
    99	  echo "freeze: DRIFT against $MANIFEST:"
   100	  python3 -I - "$MANIFEST" "$TMP" <<'PY'
   101	import sys
   102	def load(p):
   103	    m = {}
   104	    for line in open(p, encoding="utf-8"):
   105	        line = line.rstrip("\n")
   106	        if line:
   107	            h, _, rel = line.partition("  ")

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# fingerprint.sh — toolchain fingerprint for ablation runs (cycle-130 FR-4, SDD A11 / DEC-0389)
     4	#
     5	# Prints `fp:<sha256>` over the LC_ALL=C-sorted `tool=version` lines of the
     6	# toolchain an ablation run depends on (claude, codex, python3, node, yq, jq,
     7	# bats, git, docker) plus `source_tree=<HEAD of --source-tree>`. A tool that is
     8	# not installed reads `tool=absent`, so a missing tool changes the fingerprint
     9	# instead of failing the run. The value fills `image_digest` in host mode and
    10	# `fingerprint` in every mode (MANIFEST.json, pipeline.json, runs.jsonl). It reads the
    11	# HOST toolchain: in container mode the phases run on the image's toolchain, and the
    12	# image digest (not this value) identifies the batch's versions (on 2026-10-15 the host
    13	# CLI was 2.1.300 while Dockerfile.ablation pins 2.1.299).
    14	#
    15	# Usage:
    16	#   fingerprint.sh [--source-tree DIR] [--claude-bin B] [--bats-bin B] [--json]
    17	#
    18	# Options:
    19	#   --source-tree DIR  the pinned Loa tree; its `git rev-parse HEAD` is folded in
    20	#                      (`none` when absent or not a git tree)
    21	#   --claude-bin B     the CLI executable (default: $EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN, else claude)
    22	#   --bats-bin B       bats executable (default: bats on PATH, else the operator's
    23	#                      ~/.local/dotfiles/tools/diff-so-fancy/test/bats/bin/bats)
    24	#   --json             print {fingerprint, tools{}, source_tree, lines[]} instead
    25	#
    26	# Exit codes:
    27	#   0  printed
    28	#   2  usage error
    29	#
    30	# Tested by evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats (fingerprint cases).
    31	# =============================================================================
    32	set -euo pipefail
    33	export LC_ALL=C
    34	
    35	# Hashing is Python hashlib: no harness script sources .claude/ code (eval.yml
    36	# "Validate grader trust boundary").
    37	
    38	SOURCE_TREE=""
    39	CLAUDE_BIN="${EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN:-claude}"
    40	BATS_BIN="${LOA_EVAL_BATS_BIN:-}"
    41	JSON=false
    42	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    43	  case "$1" in
    44	    --source-tree) SOURCE_TREE="${2:?--source-tree needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
    45	    --claude-bin)  CLAUDE_BIN="${2:?--claude-bin needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
    46	    --bats-bin)    BATS_BIN="${2:?--bats-bin needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
    47	    --json)        JSON=true; shift ;;
    48	    -h|--help)     sed -n '2,28p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    49	    *) echo "fingerprint.sh: unknown argument: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    50	  esac
    51	done
    52	if [[ -z "$BATS_BIN" ]]; then
    53	  if command -v bats >/dev/null 2>&1; then BATS_BIN=bats
    54	  else BATS_BIN="$HOME/.local/dotfiles/tools/diff-so-fancy/test/bats/bin/bats"; fi
    55	fi
    56	
    57	# first line of `<bin> <args>`, whitespace collapsed; `absent` when not runnable
    58	tool_version() {  # tool_version <bin> <args...>
    59	  local bin="$1"; shift
    60	  if ! command -v "$bin" >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ ! -x "$bin" ]]; then printf 'absent'; return 0; fi
    61	  local out
    62	  out="$("$bin" "$@" 2>&1 < /dev/null || true)"
    63	  out="$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n '1p' | tr -s ' \t' ' ' | sed 's/^ //; s/ $//')"
    64	  [[ -n "$out" ]] || out="unknown"
    65	  printf '%s' "$out"
    66	}
    67	
    68	lines="$(
    69	  {
    70	    printf 'claude=%s\n'  "$(tool_version "$CLAUDE_BIN" --version)"
    71	    printf 'codex=%s\n'   "$(tool_version codex --version)"
    72	    printf 'python3=%s\n' "$(tool_version python3 --version)"
    73	    printf 'node=%s\n'    "$(tool_version node --version)"
    74	    printf 'yq=%s\n'      "$(tool_version yq --version)"
    75	    printf 'jq=%s\n'      "$(tool_version jq --version)"
    76	    printf 'bats=%s\n'    "$(tool_version "$BATS_BIN" --version)"
    77	    printf 'git=%s\n'     "$(tool_version git --version)"
    78	    printf 'docker=%s\n'  "$(tool_version docker --version)"
    79	  } | LC_ALL=C sort
    80	)"
    81	src="none"
    82	if [[ -n "$SOURCE_TREE" ]]; then
    83	  src="$(git -C "$SOURCE_TREE" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo none)"
    84	fi
    85	lines="$lines"$'\n'"source_tree=$src"
    86	digest="$(printf '%s\n' "$lines" | python3 -I -c 'import hashlib, sys; print(hashlib.sha256(sys.stdin.buffer.read()).hexdigest())')"
    87	fp="fp:$digest"
    88	
    89	if [[ "$JSON" == true ]]; then
    90	  printf '%s\n' "$lines" | jq -Rn --arg fp "$fp" --arg src "$src" '
    91	    [inputs | select(length > 0)] as $l
    92	    | {fingerprint: $fp, source_tree: $src, lines: $l,
    93	       tools: ($l | map(select(startswith("source_tree=") | not) | capture("^(?<k>[^=]+)=(?<v>.*)$") | {(.k): .v}) | add)}'
    94	else
    95	  printf '%s\n' "$fp"
    96	fi

     1	# Dockerfile.ablation — container executor image for the cycle-130 component ablation
     2	# (SDD D-4.9 / DEC-0411). Extends Dockerfile.sandbox's pinned base and non-root user
     3	# with the Claude Code CLI, the codex CLI, pytest and bats. It holds NO credentials.
     4	# pipeline-run.sh mounts exactly two host paths: the sandbox read-write at /workspace
     5	# and a per-run writable HOME at /home/evaluser (<run>/meta/home: the codex CLI's
     6	# auth.json/config.toml copies, empty .claude/ and .aws/; the CLI's session store). The
     7	# Bedrock route authenticates from AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK passed in the environment.
     8	# The image's tool versions (below) are the batch's versions: every arm runs here.
     9	#
    10	# Build (no build context is needed; nothing is COPY'd):
    11	#   docker build -t loa-ablation:258 - < evals/harness/Dockerfile.ablation
    12	# Run:
    13	#   evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh --executor container --image loa-ablation:258 …
    14	#   (pipeline-run.sh passes --rm --name --user --network bridge --read-only --tmpfs /tmp
    15	#    --pids-limit 512 --memory 4g --cpus 2 and exactly the two mounts)
    16	#
    17	# Digest pinned 2026-02-11 (same base as Dockerfile.sandbox):
    18	#   docker manifest inspect node:20.11.0-bookworm-slim | jq '.manifests[0].digest'
    19	FROM rust:1-bookworm AS brbuild
    20	RUN cargo install beads_rust --version 0.2.6 --root /opt/br --locked 2>/dev/null || cargo install beads_rust --version 0.2.6 --root /opt/br
    21	
    22	FROM node:20.11.0-bookworm-slim@sha256:8ea90c4f037cc3c2f566eb46c53eaac005129113487eda4090058fe554578104 AS base
    23	
    24	ARG CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=2.1.299
    25	ARG CODEX_VERSION=0.162.1
    26	ARG PYTEST_VERSION=9.0.2
    27	ARG BATS_VERSION=v1.13.0
    28	
    29	RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    30	    bash \
    31	    git \
    32	    jq \
    33	    python3 \
    34	    python3-pip \
    35	    python3-venv \
    36	    grep \
    37	    diffutils \
    38	    coreutils \
    39	    procps \
    40	    ca-certificates \
    41	    curl \
    42	    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
    43	
    44	# yq (mikefarah/yq) with SHA256 integrity verification (as Dockerfile.sandbox)
    45	ARG YQ_VERSION=v4.40.5
    46	ARG YQ_SHA256_AMD64=0d6aaf1cf44a8d18fbc7ed0ef14f735a8df8d2e314c4cc0f0242d35c0a440c95
    47	ARG YQ_SHA256_ARM64=9431f0fa39a0af03a152d7fe19a86e42e9ff28d503ed4a70598f9261ec944a97
    48	RUN arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) && \
    49	    case "$arch" in \
    50	      amd64) yq_arch="amd64"; yq_sha256="${YQ_SHA256_AMD64}" ;; \
    51	      arm64) yq_arch="arm64"; yq_sha256="${YQ_SHA256_ARM64}" ;; \
    52	      *) echo "Unsupported architecture: $arch" && exit 1 ;; \
    53	    esac && \
    54	    curl -fsSL "https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/${YQ_VERSION}/yq_linux_${yq_arch}" \
    55	      -o /usr/local/bin/yq && \
    56	    echo "${yq_sha256}  /usr/local/bin/yq" | sha256sum -c - && \
    57	    chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq
    58	
    59	# The two CLIs at the versions the fingerprint pins (exact versions, no ranges).
    60	RUN npm install -g --no-fund --no-audit \
    61	      "@anthropic-ai/claude-code@${CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION}" \
    62	      "@openai/codex@${CODEX_VERSION}" \
    63	    && npm cache clean --force
    64	
    65	# pytest for Python fixtures (bookworm's pip is externally managed)
    66	RUN pip3 install --no-cache-dir --break-system-packages "pytest==${PYTEST_VERSION}"
    67	# cheval's declared dependencies (.claude/adapters/pyproject.toml: dependencies + the `full` extra),
    68	# so the sandbox gates (adversarial-review.sh, flatline-orchestrator.sh) can dispatch (lead, DEC-0482)
    69	RUN pip3 install --no-cache-dir --break-system-packages "rfc8785>=0.1.4" "jsonschema>=4.21" "pyyaml>=6.0" "httpx[http2]>=0.24.0"
    70	
    71	# bats-core at the pinned tag
    72	RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch "${BATS_VERSION}" https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core.git /tmp/bats-core && \
    73	    /tmp/bats-core/install.sh /usr/local && \
    74	    rm -rf /tmp/bats-core
    75	
    76	# Disable npm lifecycle scripts for anything the agent installs later
    77	RUN npm config set ignore-scripts true
    78	
    79	# Non-root user (as Dockerfile.sandbox). At run time /home/evaluser is replaced by the
    80	# per-run HOME bind mount and the process runs as the host uid (--user).
    81	RUN groupadd -r evaluser && useradd -r -g evaluser -d /home/evaluser -s /bin/bash evaluser
    82	# No beads (br) in the image: beads_rust 0.2.6 is not on crates.io and the host binary needs glibc 2.38+; the sandbox
    83	# materialiser writes the beads opt-out marker (LOA_EVAL_BR_BIN unset/absent), so every arm runs the skills'
    84	# markdown fallback alike (lead, Sprint 258).
    85	RUN mkdir -p /home/evaluser/.aws /home/evaluser/.claude /home/evaluser/.codex /workspace && \
    86	    chown -R evaluser:evaluser /home/evaluser /workspace
    87	
    88	ENV TZ=UTC
    89	ENV LC_ALL=C
    90	ENV HOME=/home/evaluser
    91	ENV NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=true
    92	ENV CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1
    93	
    94	USER evaluser
    95	WORKDIR /workspace
    96	
    97	# Health check — every tool the fingerprint names is present
    98	RUN bash --version && git --version && jq --version && node --version && \
    99	    python3 --version && python3 -m pytest --version && yq --version && \
   100	    bats --version && claude --version && codex --version && \
   101	    echo "All tools verified"
   102	
   103	ENTRYPOINT []
   104	CMD ["/bin/bash"]

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/gen-checksums.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.1, DEC-0368)
     4	#
     5	# Writes the System Zone integrity manifest `.claude/checksums.json` from the
     6	# TRACKED `.claude/` tree only. The legacy generators (mount-loa.sh and
     7	# update.sh `generate_checksums`) walk the working tree with `find`, so build,
     8	# cache and runtime artefacts (`__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, `node_modules`,
     9	# `.run/`) that exist only on the generating machine end up in the manifest and
    10	# read as Missing on every fresh mount. This generator lists
    11	#
    12	#   git -C ROOT ls-files -z -- .claude
    13	#
    14	# minus every path under `.claude/overrides/` (user-owned) and minus the
    15	# manifest itself (`.claude/checksums.json`), hashes each with
    16	# `sha256_portable` (.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh) and writes
    17	#
    18	#   {"generated": "<UTC ISO-8601>", "algorithm": "sha256",
    19	#    "files": {"<path>": "<sha256 hex>", ...}}
    20	#
    21	# pretty-printed by jq (2-space), keys in `LC_ALL=C` byte order. Two runs on
    22	# the same tree are byte-identical except `generated`. The working-tree content
    23	# of each tracked path is hashed (an unstaged edit is reflected); a tracked
    24	# path deleted from the working tree is skipped with a warning on stderr.
    25	#
    26	# Usage:
    27	#   tools/gen-checksums.sh [--root DIR] [--out FILE]   # (re)generate
    28	#   tools/gen-checksums.sh --check [--root DIR] [--out FILE]
    29	#
    30	# Options:
    31	#   --root DIR   repository work tree to read (default: the git top level of
    32	#                the current directory)
    33	#   --out FILE   manifest path (default: ROOT/.claude/checksums.json). With
    34	#                --check this is the committed manifest that is compared.
    35	#   --check      regenerate to a temp file and compare its `files` map with
    36	#                the manifest at --out; nothing is written
    37	#   -h, --help   this text
    38	#
    39	# Exit codes:
    40	#   0  generated, or --check: the `files` maps are identical
    41	#   1  --check: drift (the first ten differing paths, each labelled added /
    42	#      removed / changed, on stderr) or the manifest is absent / not JSON
    43	#   2  usage error, ROOT is not a git work tree, or a tracked path name that
    44	#      cannot be represented safely (newline, tab or backslash)
    45	# =============================================================================
    46	set -euo pipefail
    47	export LC_ALL=C
    48	
    49	SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    50	# shellcheck source=../.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh
    51	source "${SELF_DIR}/../.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"
    52	
    53	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    54	die2() { echo "gen-checksums: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    55	
    56	MANIFEST_REL=".claude/checksums.json"
    57	ROOT=""
    58	OUT=""
    59	CHECK=0
    60	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    61	  case "$1" in
    62	    --check) CHECK=1; shift ;;
    63	    --root)
    64	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--root requires a directory"
    65	      ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    66	    --out)
    67	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--out requires a file path"
    68	      OUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    69	    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    70	    *) die2 "unknown argument: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    71	  esac
    72	done
    73	
    74	if [[ -z "$ROOT" ]]; then
    75	  ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "not inside a git work tree (use --root DIR)"
    76	fi
    77	[[ -d "$ROOT" ]] || die2 "--root is not a directory: $ROOT"
    78	ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd -P)"
    79	[[ "$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree 2>/dev/null || true)" == "true" ]] \
    80	  || die2 "not a git work tree: $ROOT"
    81	[[ -n "$OUT" ]] || OUT="${ROOT}/${MANIFEST_REL}"
    82	
    83	TMP_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gen-checksums.XXXXXX")"
    84	cleanup() { rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"; }
    85	trap cleanup EXIT
    86	
    87	# --- 1. the tracked set (NUL-safe, C-sorted, overrides and manifest removed) --
    88	files=()
    89	while IFS= read -r -d '' path; do
    90	  case "$path" in
    91	    .claude/overrides/*|"$MANIFEST_REL") continue ;;
    92	  esac
    93	  case "$path" in
    94	    *$'\n'*|*$'\t'*|*\\*) die2 "refusing a tracked path with a newline, tab or backslash: $(printf '%q' "$path")" ;;
    95	  esac
    96	  if [[ ! -f "${ROOT}/${path}" ]]; then
    97	    # A gitlink, a dangling symlink or a path deleted in the working tree.
    98	    echo "gen-checksums: warning: tracked path not a file in the working tree, skipped: $path" >&2
    99	    continue
   100	  fi
   101	  files+=("$path")
   102	done < <(git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -z -- .claude | sort -z)
   103	
   104	# --- 2. hash in chunks (one sha256 process per 400 paths, order preserved) ----
   105	TSV="${TMP_DIR}/files.tsv"
   106	: > "$TSV"
   107	n=${#files[@]}
   108	i=0
   109	while [[ $i -lt $n ]]; do
   110	  chunk=("${files[@]:i:400}")
   111	  hashes=()
   112	  while IFS= read -r line; do
   113	    hashes+=("${line%% *}")
   114	  done < <(cd "$ROOT" && sha256_portable "${chunk[@]}")
   115	  [[ ${#hashes[@]} -eq ${#chunk[@]} ]] || die2 "sha256 returned ${#hashes[@]} digests for ${#chunk[@]} paths"
   116	  j=0
   117	  while [[ $j -lt ${#chunk[@]} ]]; do
   118	    [[ "${hashes[j]}" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || die2 "unexpected sha256 output for ${chunk[j]}"
   119	    printf '%s\t%s\n' "${chunk[j]}" "${hashes[j]}" >> "$TSV"
   120	    j=$((j + 1))
   121	  done
   122	  i=$((i + 400))
   123	done
   124	[[ $n -gt 0 ]] || echo "gen-checksums: warning: no tracked files under .claude in $ROOT" >&2
   125	
   126	GEN="${TMP_DIR}/checksums.json"
   127	jq -Rn --arg generated "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" '
   128	  {generated: $generated, algorithm: "sha256",
   129	   files: ([inputs | select(length > 0) | split("\t") | {key: .[0], value: .[1]}] | from_entries)}
   130	' < "$TSV" > "$GEN"
   131	
   132	# --- 3a. write ----------------------------------------------------------------
   133	if [[ $CHECK -eq 0 ]]; then
   134	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
   135	  chmod 0644 "$GEN"
   136	  # mv replaces a symlinked manifest instead of writing through it.
   137	  mv -f "$GEN" "$OUT"
   138	  echo "gen-checksums: wrote $n entries to $OUT" >&2
   139	  exit 0
   140	fi
   141	
   142	# --- 3b. --check --------------------------------------------------------------
   143	if [[ ! -f "$OUT" ]]; then
   144	  echo "gen-checksums: --check: manifest not found: $OUT (run tools/gen-checksums.sh)" >&2
   145	  exit 1
   146	fi
   147	if ! jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$OUT" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   148	  echo "gen-checksums: --check: manifest is not JSON with a files object: $OUT" >&2
   149	  exit 1
   150	fi
   151	DIFF="${TMP_DIR}/diff.txt"
   152	jq -rn --slurpfile old "$OUT" --slurpfile new "$GEN" '
   153	  ($old[0].files) as $o | ($new[0].files) as $n |
   154	  ( [ $n | keys[] | . as $p | select($o | has($p) | not) | {p: $p, k: "added"} ]
   155	  + [ $o | keys[] | . as $p | select($n | has($p) | not) | {p: $p, k: "removed"} ]
   156	  + [ $n | keys[] | . as $p | select(($o | has($p)) and $o[$p] != $n[$p]) | {p: $p, k: "changed"} ] )
   157	  | sort_by(.p) | .[] | "\(.k): \(.p)"
   158	' > "$DIFF"
   159	count=$(wc -l < "$DIFF" | tr -d ' ')
   160	if [[ "$count" -eq 0 ]]; then
   161	  echo "gen-checksums: --check: OK ($n entries match $OUT)" >&2
   162	  exit 0
   163	fi
   164	echo "gen-checksums: --check: DRIFT — $count path(s) differ between $OUT and the tracked tree:" >&2
   165	sed -n '1,10s/^/  /p' "$DIFF" >&2
   166	[[ "$count" -le 10 ]] || echo "  ... and $((count - 10)) more" >&2
   167	echo "gen-checksums: regenerate with: bash tools/gen-checksums.sh" >&2
   168	exit 1
